topSignals.title: Bloom Energy closes at $184.89 (-14.9%) — two-day fuel cell rout deepens ahead of Q2 earnings
topSignals.text: — On July 25 (Friday), BE added a further -14.9% decline (volume: 15.8M shares, +29.5% above the 65-day average) to close at $184.89, extending a -13% drop on July 24 that also pulled down FuelCell Energy (-9%) and Plug Power (-4%). BE is now ~47% below the June 17-18 all-time high of $351; the YTD gain has collapsed from +219% at the peak to approximately +98%. Core bear thesis: Bloom's FY2026 guidance midpoint ($3.6B) requires approximately $1.04B/quarter in H2 given Q1 actuals ($751M) and consensus Q2 ($828M) — a step-change acceleration that Oracle Jupiter's unresolved permitting makes increasingly uncertain. Q2 earnings Monday July 28 (after close): consensus $828.4M revenue / $0.41 EPS; options pricing a 32.4% post-earnings swing. At $184.89, BE now trades below all 12 analyst price targets for the first time. ts2.tech | 24/7 Wall St. July 24 selloff

topSignals.title: Oracle Project Jupiter gas pipeline rejected for a SECOND TIME (NM Land Commissioner, July 20)
topSignals.text: — New Mexico Land Commissioner Garcia Richard denied Energy Transfer's Green Chile pipeline application for the second time on July 20, 2026. The pipeline — designed to carry 400 MMcf/day to fuel 2.45 GW of Bloom SOFCs — is blocked from crossing state land; objections cite water use, CO2 emissions, and insufficient state revenue. A third application, alternative land route, or federal easement is now required. Simultaneously, the NM Environment Department has scheduled a public hearing on the air quality permit, with a final decision deadline in late November 2026. Two sequential prerequisites (gas supply + air quality permit) remain unresolved. SemiAnalysis has revised its base-case first-power estimate from 2027 to 2029. Pete Dinelli (2nd rejection) | DCD | Seeking Alpha

topSignals.title: NERC Level 3 Essential Action Alert — 7 computational-load compliance actions due August 3
topSignals.text: — NERC issued a Level 3 ("Essential Action") alert directing all registered entities to implement seven immediate compliance measures for computational load integration: modeling, studies, instrumentation, commissioning, operations, protection, and control. Deadline: August 3, 2026 — eight days away. This is the fastest-moving consequence of FERC's July 16 Docket RD26-7-000 order (covered July 24 digest). Grid-dependent data center operators now face mandatory near-term NERC compliance; on-site SOFC islanded generation substantially avoids this burden, adding a new avoided-compliance-cost line to the self-supply value case. NERC newsroom | RTO Insider

items.text: Elcogen: Quiet. No EFCF 2026 proceedings published (day 22+ embargo). E3000 G2 deliveries confirmed underway per elcogen.com product page; ELCO I factory (360 MW/yr, Tallinn) in volume production. Additional context (first appearance): EU Commission Executive VP Teresa Ribera visited the Tallinn facility in June 2026, confirming political-level visibility of the ELCO I ramp. Watch: elcogen.com for EFCF data; ELCO I throughput update in Q3.

Topsoe: Quiet on new SOFC/SOEC data-center orders. Herning SOEC factory hibernation and 440-job cut unchanged. New context (first appearance): Topsoe was selected to deliver 120 MW SOEC technology for Carbon Neutral Fuels' Project Starling — an e-sustainable aviation fuel project in Workington, UK; construction planned 2028, operations target 2031, pending FID. Topsoe's electrolyzer demonstration plant continues to deliver strong results per company communications. H2 fuel pathway for SOFC data-center deployments remains deferred to 2029+; NG/biogas base case confirmed for LCOE modeling. Topsoe/Carbon Neutral Fuels

Oracle Project Jupiter (2.45 GW) — Second pipeline rejection confirmed as the central near-term execution risk (see Top Signal #2). Without a resolved gas supply route, Bloom cannot fuel the 2.45 GW SOFC campus. Timeline now open-ended; SemiAnalysis base-case first power 2029. Oracle has not issued a formal timeline update.

Active pipeline (unchanged): Crusoe/Cheyenne (900 MW Phase 1, Bloom, H2 2026 target), FCEL/Fit Energy (30 MW initial delivery H2 2026, 350 MW option), Equinix (>100 MW), AEP/Bloom (1 GW, Wyoming, 2030), Bloom/Brookfield ($25B framework), Nebius/IDF/Oaktree ($1.7B). EdgeMode Malpica 300 MW Bloom SOFC Spain — Spark AI Foundry NBO €300M (covered July 24) status unchanged.

NERC Level 3 Essential Action Alert (August 3 deadline) — See Top Signal #3. Seven mandatory compliance actions for computational loads due from all NERC-registered entities. ISO-NE abeyance filing deadline also August 3. Full FERC RM26-4 tariff reform filings from all RTOs/ISOs due August 17.

NY EO 62 moratorium (active, no new developments): The one-year ban on new hyperscale DCs (≥50 MW) in New York signed July 14 remains in effect. Senators Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez have introduced federal legislation (first mention) to apply a similar moratorium nationally — status pending committee review. CNBC | AOL/Sanders-AOC bill
Quiet otherwise. No new EU CADA, Germany EnEfG, ERCOT, or Virginia legislative developments.

~50% of planned 2026 US data center builds face delays or cancellation — July 24 industry analysis confirms that roughly half of planned 2026 US data-center capacity will be delayed or cancelled, driven by interconnection queue backlog, permitting resistance (NM, NY), and AI capex uncertainty. This structural shortfall is a sustained macro-level tailwind for SOFC on-site self-supply deployments that bypass the grid entirely.

Bulletin of Atomic Scientists (July 24): "Don't fall for Big Tech's nuclear PR hype" — Independent expert consensus unchanged: nuclear power for AI data centers is a post-2030 story at best; relicensed large light-water units (TMI, Calpine fleet) are the only near-term play; SMRs remain commercially viable mid-2030s earliest. No competitive threat to SOFC before 2030. Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
Quiet otherwise. No new CCGT, battery, or PEM announcements.

Delta Electronics Taiwan SOFC/SOEC factory — NT$6.95 billion (~$215M) factory site acquired by Delta in Taiwan for large-scale manufacturing of Ceres-licensed solid oxide hydrogen energy solutions (SOFC + SOEC), with production scheduled to start by end-2026. Expands the Asian Ceres licensing ecosystem as an alternative non-US SOFC supply pathway alongside Doosan (Korea). Ceres PR | World-Energy.org

lcoe.text: Oracle Jupiter second rejection — delayed capex scale curve: 2.45 GW now likely 2029+. Bloom Fremont 2 GW/yr factory at lower-than-planned utilization 2027-2028 delays volume-driven cost reduction. Add "low-utilization" scenario: Bloom at ~40-60% capacity factor 2027-2028, pushing the $4,000-4,500/kW capex milestone from 2027 to 2029.

BE at $184.89 — H2 guidance validation on July 28 (Monday): Revenue needs $1.04B/quarter in H2 to hit guidance midpoint. A Q2 miss or reduced H2 guidance would trigger a further revision of the capex-reduction timeline. Key inputs from the Q2 call: (a) manufacturing cost/kW at Fremont, (b) product gross margin vs. ~34%, (c) Oracle Jupiter / AEP Wyoming timeline updates, (d) any EaaS $/MWh pricing disclosure.

NERC computational-load compliance — $3-12/MWh avoided-cost benefit for SOFC self-supply: NERC Level 3 alert + December 31 mandatory standards create ongoing compliance overhead for grid-tied DC operators (modeling, instrumentation, reporting, potential curtailment obligations). By analogy with NERC CIP standards: estimated $3-10M/yr for large operators, translating to $3-12/MWh at 100 MW / 8,760 h/yr. Add as a positive adjustment line in SOFC vs. grid LCOE comparison.
Topsoe Project Starling (120 MW SOEC, 2031): e-SAF/green-H2 application; no near-term impact on SOFC data-center LCOE. NG/biogas base case confirmed for all near-to-medium-term SOFC scenarios.
